bug_semantics: Authenticated stored XSS in Akaunting's reusable delete-confirmation flow (CWE-79). A user who can create or edit records (e.g. Items; request rule name=required|string only) persists HTML/JavaScript in the record name. DeleteLink::getMessage() at 3.1.21 interpolates that name into trans('general.delete_confirm') inside a HTML snippet after only addslashes() and quote-to-" replacement, which does not encode <, >, or event-handler markup. resources/views/components/delete-link.blade.php then emits the message with {!! $message !!} into data-message. global.js onDeleteViaConfirmation reads the attribute and confirmDelete passes it to AkauntingModal.vue, which renders it with v-html, so a payload such as executes in another authenticated user's session when they open the delete dialog.
flaw_origin:
The XSS mechanism is the first public write of an unescaped model name wrapped in HTML and handed to confirmDelete, which concatenates the message into a modal HTML string and appends it to the DOM. That pair first appears in the repository root commit 515bdaf5cd435a4bad54802dc0c814462586275e (2017-09-14, denisdulici, message 'first commit'): resources/views/partials/form/delete_button.blade.php line 16 uses '' . $item->$value . '' with no HTML encoding, and public/js/app.js confirmDelete builds '

' + message + '

' then $('body').append(html).
